Jq85u_y_UCM.text: A short walk right after you eat can do more for your blood sugar than a long walk later in the day. After a meal, the sugar from your food pours into your blood. It usually reaches its peak about an hour or so after you eat. Here's the trick. Your muscles are the biggest sugar users in your body. When your legs start moving, your muscle cells open tiny doors and pull sugar straight out of your blood. They don't even need much insulin to do it. So the spike comes up lower and goes down faster. ioPRAQav8y4.first_3s: When this fish gets touched, it releases a thick, sticky slime that
ioPRAQav8y4.text: When this fish gets touched, it releases a thick, sticky slime that can turn the water into a slimy mess. It's called a hagfish, and it can fill the surrounding water with slime in just seconds. When attacked by a predator, it releases a special slime that can expand up to 10 ,000 times its original volume. This slime can clog the predator's gills, forcing it to give up and swim away. But here's the clever part. To avoid getting trapped in its own slime, the hagfish twists its body into a knot and slides through it to wipe the slime away. That's one seriously slimy survival trick.
